texts.0287a46dcc78: 1. To investigate whether a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes in childhood or young adult life continues to incur an increased risk of an early death compared to the general population.  (A previous study in Yorkshire and others in the UK have established a raised risk in earlier cohorts).2. To identify factors potentially associated with early mortality from type 1 diabetes such as length of diabetes, type of diabetes, sex, socioeconomic status, urban/rural residence or ethnicity.3.  To provide anonymised data for a pan European study (EURODIAB) of mortality associated with a diagnosis of diabetes in childhood for the purpose of international comparison. 4.  To investigate for the first time in the UK whether type 2 diabetes in young people (diagnosed under 30 years) carries with it an increased mortality.
